title: MySQL
label: MySQL
desc: Open source relational database with InnoDB transactions, replication and a large SQL dialect.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install MySQL, start the service and secure the first account.

snippets.code:
# Debian or Ubuntu
sudo apt update
sudo apt install mysql-server
sudo systemctl enable --now mysql
sudo mysql_secure_installation

# macOS with Homebrew
brew install mysql
brew services start mysql
mysql_secure_installation

# Confirm that the service is running and see the client version
sudo systemctl status mysql
mysql --version

# First login through the administrative system account
sudo mysql

sections.title: Connection
sections.description: Open a session from the client and inspect what it is connected to.

snippets.code:
# Connect as a local user; -p prompts for the password
mysql -u app_user -p

# Connect to a database on another host and port
mysql -h 192.168.1.20 -P 3306 -u app_user -p inventory

# Run one statement and exit
mysql -u app_user -p -e "SELECT VERSION(), CURRENT_USER();" inventory

# Execute a script against a database
mysql -u app_user -p inventory < schema.sql

sections.title: Databases and Tables
sections.description: Create the schema and the tables used throughout this sheet.

snippets.code:
CREATE TABLE products (
  id           BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  sku          VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
  name         VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  price_cents  INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  stock        INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  discontinued TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  notes        VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  created_at   TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  UNIQUE KEY uq_products_sku (sku)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE customers (
  id        BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  email     VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  full_name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  UNIQUE KEY uq_customers_email (email)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id          BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  customer_id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  status      ENUM('pending','paid','shipped','cancelled') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  total_cents INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  placed_at   DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  KEY idx_orders_customer (customer_id),
  CONSTRAINT fk_orders_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE order_items (
  order_id         BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  product_id       BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  quantity         SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  unit_price_cents INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id),
  CONSTRAINT fk_items_order FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES orders (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT fk_items_product FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products (id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

sections.title: Data Types
sections.description: Pick the column type that matches the values you store.

snippets.code:
-- Integers
TINYINT        -- 1 byte, -128 to 127
SMALLINT       -- 2 bytes
MEDIUMINT      -- 3 bytes
INT            -- 4 bytes
BIGINT         -- 8 bytes
INT UNSIGNED   -- 0 to 4294967295

-- Exact and approximate numbers
DECIMAL(10,2)  -- exact, 10 digits in total with 2 after the point
FLOAT          -- 4-byte approximate number
DOUBLE         -- 8-byte approximate number

-- Strings and binary data
CHAR(2)        -- fixed length, padded with spaces
VARCHAR(255)   -- variable length, at most 255 characters
TEXT           -- up to 65535 bytes
BLOB           -- binary large object

-- Date and time
DATE           -- 1000-01-01 to 9999-12-31
DATETIME       -- date and time without time zone conversion
TIMESTAMP      -- stored in UTC, 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-19
TIME           -- -838:59:59 to 838:59:59
YEAR           -- four-digit year

-- Other common choices
BOOLEAN        -- alias for TINYINT(1), values 0 and 1
JSON           -- validated JSON document
ENUM('draft','live')  -- one value from a fixed list

sections.title: Inserting Rows
sections.description: Add one row or many, skip duplicates or overwrite them.

snippets.code:
-- Upsert: update the existing row instead of failing (MySQL 8.0.19+)
INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price_cents, stock)
VALUES ('KB-1000', 'Mechanical Keyboard', 11900, 5) AS new_row
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
  price_cents = new_row.price_cents,
  stock = products.stock + new_row.stock;

-- Copy rows from one table into another
INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price_cents, stock)
SELECT sku, name, price_cents, stock
FROM archived_products
WHERE discontinued = 0;

sections.title: Selecting Rows
sections.description: Read columns, compute values and page through the result.

snippets.code:
-- First page: 10 rows
SELECT id, name, price_cents
FROM products
ORDER BY id
LIMIT 10;

-- Third page: skip 20 rows, then take 10
SELECT id, name, price_cents
FROM products
ORDER BY id
LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20;

-- Always pair OFFSET with ORDER BY, or the page boundaries are arbitrary
SELECT id, name FROM products ORDER BY name LIMIT 5 OFFSET 0;

sections.title: Filtering and Sorting
sections.description: Narrow rows with WHERE and control order with ORDER BY.

snippets.code:
SELECT id, name, price_cents
FROM products
WHERE stock > 0
  AND price_cents BETWEEN 1000 AND 10000
  AND sku LIKE 'KB-%';

-- Either condition is enough
SELECT id, name FROM products
WHERE stock = 0 OR discontinued = 1;

-- Match any value in a list
SELECT id, name FROM products
WHERE sku IN ('KB-1000', 'MS-2000');

-- NULL never equals anything, so test it with IS NULL
SELECT id, name FROM products
WHERE notes IS NULL;

-- Most expensive first; ties sorted by name
SELECT id, name, price_cents
FROM products
WHERE discontinued = 0
ORDER BY price_cents DESC, name ASC
LIMIT 5;

-- Sort by an expression
SELECT name, price_cents * stock AS inventory_value_cents
FROM products
ORDER BY inventory_value_cents DESC;

-- Case-insensitive contains match
SELECT id, name FROM products
WHERE name LIKE '%keyboard%';

sections.title: Joins
sections.description: Combine related tables and keep unmatched rows when needed.

snippets.code:
-- Inner join: only customers that have at least one order
SELECT c.full_name, o.id AS order_id, o.total_cents
FROM customers AS c
INNER JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
ORDER BY o.placed_at DESC;

-- Left join: keep customers without orders, counted as zero
SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.full_name
ORDER BY order_count DESC;

-- Find the customers with no order at all
SELECT c.full_name
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;

-- Walk order_items back to products and orders
SELECT p.sku, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold
FROM order_items AS oi
JOIN products AS p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders AS o ON o.id = oi.order_id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY p.id, p.sku
ORDER BY units_sold DESC;

-- Self join: pair each product with every cheaper product
SELECT a.name AS product, b.name AS cheaper_product
FROM products AS a
JOIN products AS b ON b.price_cents < a.price_cents
ORDER BY a.name, b.price_cents DESC;

sections.title: Aggregation and Grouping
sections.description: Collapse rows into counts, sums and per-group totals.

snippets.code:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_products,
       AVG(price_cents) AS avg_price_cents,
       MIN(price_cents) AS cheapest_cents,
       MAX(price_cents) AS most_expensive_cents,
       SUM(stock) AS units_in_stock
FROM products;

-- COUNT(column) ignores NULL, COUNT(*) does not
SELECT COUNT(*) AS all_rows,
       COUNT(notes) AS rows_with_notes,
       COUNT(DISTINCT stock) AS distinct_stock_values
FROM products;

SELECT status,
       COUNT(*) AS orders,
       SUM(total_cents) AS revenue_cents
FROM orders
GROUP BY status
HAVING SUM(total_cents) > 100000
ORDER BY revenue_cents DESC;

-- WITH ROLLUP adds a grand-total row where status is NULL
SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY status WITH ROLLUP;

-- One row per customer, with their order count and lifetime value
SELECT customer_id,
       COUNT(*) AS orders,
       SUM(total_cents) AS spent_cents
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id;

sections.title: Subqueries
sections.description: Use a query as a value, a list, a table or a named CTE.

snippets.code:
-- Scalar subquery: compare against the average
SELECT name, price_cents
FROM products
WHERE price_cents > (SELECT AVG(price_cents) FROM products);

-- IN with a subquery that returns one column
SELECT full_name
FROM customers
WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid');

-- EXISTS stops at the first matching row
SELECT c.full_name
FROM customers AS c
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o
  WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.total_cents > 50000
);

-- Derived table: aggregate over a query result
SELECT status, ROUND(AVG(order_total), 2) AS avg_total
FROM (
  SELECT status, total_cents / 100 AS order_total
  FROM orders
) AS per_order
GROUP BY status;

-- CTE (MySQL 8.0+) gives the subquery a name
WITH paid AS (
  SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_cents) AS spent_cents
  FROM orders
  WHERE status = 'paid'
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.full_name, paid.spent_cents
FROM customers AS c
JOIN paid ON paid.customer_id = c.id
ORDER BY paid.spent_cents DESC;

sections.title: Updating and Deleting
sections.description: Change or remove rows, alone or through a join.

snippets.code:
UPDATE products
SET price_cents = 11900,
    stock = stock - 1
WHERE sku = 'KB-1000';

-- Different changes per row with CASE
UPDATE products
SET stock = CASE
  WHEN stock < 5 THEN stock + 20
  ELSE stock + 5
END
WHERE discontinued = 0;

-- UPDATE through a join
UPDATE orders AS o
JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = o.customer_id
SET o.status = 'cancelled'
WHERE c.email = 'ana@example.com'
  AND o.status = 'pending';

sections.title: Backup and Restore
sections.description: Dump a database to a file and load it back.

snippets.code:
# Consistent dump of one InnoDB database, with routines and triggers
mysqldump -u root -p --single-transaction --routines --triggers \
  inventory > inventory-2026-11-04.sql

# Every database plus the user accounts
mysqldump -u root -p --all-databases --routines --events > all-2026-11-04.sql

# Schema only, no rows
mysqldump -u root -p --no-data inventory > inventory-schema.sql

# Restore into an existing database
mysql -u root -p inventory < inventory-2026-11-04.sql

# Compress in the pipe to save disk space
mysqldump -u root -p --single-transaction inventory | gzip > inventory.sql.gz
gunzip < inventory.sql.gz | mysql -u root -p inventory

sections.title: EXPLAIN and Performance
sections.description: Read the query plan and find the step that scans too much.

snippets.code:
EXPLAIN
SELECT c.full_name, o.total_cents
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
ORDER BY o.placed_at DESC;

-- The key column shows the index used, rows estimates the work
EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON
SELECT id FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';

-- Extra warnings about the plan or the statement
SHOW WARNINGS;

sections.title: Built-in Functions
sections.description: Ready-made helpers for strings, numbers, dates, NULL and JSON.

snippets.code:
SELECT CONCAT('Order ', id, ' for ', customer_id) AS label,
       UPPER('mysql') AS upper_text,
       LENGTH('café') AS bytes,
       CHAR_LENGTH('café') AS characters,
       SUBSTRING('2026-11-04', 1, 7) AS month,
       REPLACE('a-b-c', '-', '/') AS swapped,
       TRIM('  padded  ') AS trimmed;

SELECT ROUND(12.3456, 2) AS rounded,
       CEIL(4.1) AS rounded_up,
       FLOOR(4.9) AS rounded_down,
       MOD(17, 5) AS remainder,
       ABS(-42) AS absolute_value;

SELECT NOW() AS now,
       CURDATE() AS today,
       DATE_ADD('2026-11-04', INTERVAL 30 DAY) AS in_30_days,
       DATEDIFF('2026-12-31', '2026-11-04') AS days_left,
       DATE_FORMAT('2026-11-04', '%Y-%m-%d') AS formatted,
       UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2026-11-04 00:00:00') AS epoch;

-- NULL handling and casting
SELECT COALESCE(NULL, 'fallback') AS first_non_null,
       IFNULL(NULL, 0) AS zero,
       CAST('42' AS UNSIGNED) AS number_value,
       CAST(42 AS CHAR) AS text_value;

-- JSON extraction (MySQL 5.7+)
SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('{"sku":"KB-1000","stock":12}', '$.stock') AS stock,
       JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT('{"sku":"KB-1000"}', '$.sku')) AS sku,
       '{"sku":"MS-2000"}'->>'$.sku' AS sku_with_arrow;

sections.title: Common Errors
sections.description: Messages you will meet, what causes them and how to fix them.

snippets.code:
ERROR 1045 (28000): Access denied for user 'app_user'@'localhost' (using password: YES)
  Cause: wrong password, or the account is not allowed from this host.
  Fix:   ALTER USER 'app_user'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'N3w-Passw0rd!';

ERROR 2002 (HY000): Can't connect to local MySQL server through socket '/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock' (2)
  Cause: the server is stopped, or the client uses another socket path.
  Fix:   sudo systemctl start mysql; SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'socket';

ERROR 1040 (08004): Too many connections
  Cause: max_connections is exhausted by open clients.
  Fix:   SET GLOBAL max_connections = 300;

ERROR 1129 (HY000): Host '10.0.0.42' is blocked because of many connection errors
  Cause: repeated failed handshakes triggered the host cache.
  Fix:   FLUSH HOSTS; and correct the credentials first.

ERROR 1062 (23000): Duplicate entry 'KB-1000' for key 'products.uq_products_sku'
  Cause: a UNIQUE index already holds that value.
  Fix:   use ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, or choose another sku.

ERROR 1054 (42S22): Unknown column 'price' in 'field list'
  Cause: the column is named price_cents, or an alias is out of scope.
  Fix:   DESCRIBE products; and use the real column name.

ERROR 1215 (HY000): Cannot add foreign key constraint
  Cause: column types or collations differ, or the parent key is not indexed.
  Fix:   make both columns BIGINT UNSIGNED and create the parent key first.

ERROR 1364 (HY000): Field 'customer_id' doesn't have a default value
  Cause: strict mode rejects an INSERT that omits a NOT NULL column.
  Fix:   supply the value, or make the column nullable.

ERROR 1265 (01000): Data truncated for column 'status' at row 1
  Cause: the value is not a member of the ENUM.
  Fix:   use 'pending', 'paid', 'shipped' or 'cancelled'.
